chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ubays ibn Hisham from al-Hasan ibn 'Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the day in which there is doubt, for people claim that whoever fasts it is like the one who breaks fast for a day from the month of Ramadan. He said: 'They are lying. If it is a day from the month of Ramadan, then it is a day they were guided to, and if it is from the others, then it is like the days that have passed.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: Equivalent to / In the rank of
key_terms.وُفِّقُوا لَهُ: They were guided to it / It was made easy for them

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the Day of Doubt (Yawm al-Shakk) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the juristic ruling on the 'Day of Doubt' (30th of Sha'ban) is clarified to counter the popular belief that its fast carries the weight of Ramadan. The Imam distinguishes between the two possibilities: if it is Ramadan, the fast is valid and accepted as a day they were guided to observe; if not, it is merely a voluntary fast with no special merit. This highlights the Shia principle of avoiding excessive caution (ihtiyat) that equates the Day of Doubt with Ramadan, emphasizing that the fast's status depends on actual confirmation rather than mere possibility.
